summary: Brick light at Escanaba, Michigan, first lit 1868 under keeper Mary Terry; discontinued 1939; restored and run as a museum by the Delta County Historical Society.

access.note: Grounds open; museum and lighthouse open in summer per the Society

facts.agency: Delta County Historical Society (operates the site; lease from the Coast Guard per the Society; LighthouseFriends says owned by the Society since 1998)

events.note: Congress appropriates $5,000 for a light on Sand Point; the land title is not clear
Station built at a cost of $11,000 (Mining Gazette) or $11K (Society)
Light first shown 13 May 1868 under keeper Mary Terry
Fire in the keeper's dwelling; keeper Mary Terry killed; 4 March 1886 (LighthouseFriends) or 5 March (Mining Gazette)
Repairs 1 April to 31 May 1886 at a cost of $2,362.72; light back at the opening of navigation
Fog bell struck by machinery; bell struck 18 April 1900 and in operation from 1 May 1900
Bell tower brought from the discontinued Tail Point light station
Illuminant changed to electricity on 1 July 1913; intensity increased from 130 to 500 candlepower
Coast Guard takes over the navigational lights
Light discontinued; served mariners from 1868 until 1939 (Society)
Coast Guard builds a crib light offshore; still in use
Coast Guard decides to stop using the building as a residence and considers razing it; the Society negotiates a lease and fundraises
Restored lighthouse opens to the public
LighthouseFriends says ownership passed to the Society; the Society describes a Coast Guard lease (disputed)
Replica fourth-order Fresnel lens installed in the lantern room

notes_for_editor: No NRHP nomination: NPGallery 97001474 is an undigitised placeholder; the 1997/1999 NRHP listings and the Michigan State Historic Site status are in the record but not used. The Board's 1866 and 1886 reports are not in the local corpus (its Lighthouse Board volumes run 1891-1901); the 1886 fire is quoted as LighthouseFriends prints it and should be checked against the 1886 volume. Conflicts left in the text: fire date (4 March per LighthouseFriends, 5 March per the Mining Gazette); Peterson's death (1913 per LighthouseFriends, April 1912 per the Mining Gazette); John Terry's death (April 1868 per LighthouseFriends, consumption per the Mining Gazette); light colour (fixed red per the Society, fixed white per LighthouseFriends); end of station operation (1939 per the Society and USLHS, 1938 per the Mining Gazette); ownership (a Coast Guard lease per the Society, transfer in 1998 per LighthouseFriends, technically Coast Guard per the Mining Gazette); summer hours (1 to 4 pm per the Society, 11 to 4 pm per LighthouseFriends and the Mining Gazette). The Board passages from the 1893, 1896-97 and 1900 volumes are read from the corpus OCR index; the 1893 and 1896-97 printed pages are not confirmed, so scan pages are cited. The USLHS roster has 29 Coast Guard lines (1960-1975) under a 'USCG' heading with no role; they are in the research JSON only, as the archive prints them, and are not named in the prose. Other station names: Peter J. Peterson to Wind Point (us-wi-wind-point), Soren Kristiansen to the Eleven Foot Shoal lightship (us-mi-eleven-foot-shoal), both from LighthouseFriends. The record's Sand Point in Baraga (us-mi-sand-point-baraga) is a different station and was not used. Focal height: the USLHS record gives 44 ft above mean high water, and LighthouseFriends gives 44 ft (13.4 m), so the value 13.4 m is used; an earlier note wrongly gave the record as 13.7 m. The research date is 2026-10-27, not 2026-10-22 as the batch note says. Fact-check additions (2026-10-22 check): the 1896-97 Board entry quoted for Escanaba is an extract from several earlier annual reports, so the story attributes it to the 1896-97 report as a quotation of earlier reports. The 'grew up on iron ore' sentence was cited to the 1921 estimate, which does not say it; the story now cites LighthouseFriends for the 1862 railroad and iron-ore founding.
